transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

After losing the job opportunity I was counting on, I feel like I’ve been reacting badly to everything and can’t cope with what’s happening in my life. It just feels like everything has been completely derailed and I don't know how to handle it.
Have you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy since this job opportunity fell through?

Yes, definitely. I actually backed out of organizing the Harvard summer fair and completely stopped going to my regular improv meet-ups, which I used to love. Now, instead of doing any of that, I just find myself canceling plans and lying around.
Do you often find yourself thinking about what you could have done differently to get that job, or feeling guilty about not being able to cope with the loss of this opportunity?

I don't think I could have done anything differently, since the organization abruptly lost its funding and froze all hiring. I don't really feel guilty, but I just feel completely overwhelmed and frozen by my inability to cope with everything being thrown off course.
How long have you been feeling overwhelmed and disconnected from your usual activities since the job opportunity fell through?

It’s been about two months now, ever since I found out the nonprofit job wasn't happening. All of this really started within a few weeks of getting the news about the hiring freeze, and I've felt unable to cope ever since.

Can you describe how your feelings of being overwhelmed and disconnected from activities have changed or evolved over these past two months, have they been steadily present or have you noticed any fluctuations?

It has been pretty steady and persistent ever since it started, mostly because my life is still completely up in the air with my lease, student loans, and lack of stable work. I feel like this reaction is directly tied to all this current uncertainty, and I really hope it will improve once I can get my situation sorted out.
Do you think you would start enjoying your activities again and feel more in control if your life situation improved, such as finding a new job or resolving your housing and financial issues?

Yes, absolutely. I keep telling myself that once I sort out a stable job or figure out a new plan, this overwhelming reaction won't go on forever. It really feels directly tied to everything being so up in the air right now, rather than being some kind of long-standing issue.

Do you feel like your emotional state and inability to cope would persist even after your current life situation improves, or do you think they would significantly improve once your external circumstances change?

I definitely think things will significantly improve once my circumstances change. I keep telling myself this won't go on forever and that once I sort out a stable job or a concrete plan, I'll be able to cope again. It really feels tied to everything being up in the air right now rather than some permanent, long-standing issue.

Do you think that if you were to face another significant setback or stressor in the future, you would likely experience a similar overwhelming reaction, or do you believe you would be able to cope better?

I believe I would be able to cope much better in the future. This extreme reaction is really just because everything hit me at once—the job falling through, my lease ending, and my student loans coming due. Once I find some stability, I don't think a future setback would derail me like this, as it feels very specific to this overwhelming transition.

You mentioned that you believe you would cope better with future setbacks once you've found stability, but can you tell me more about what you think is different about your current situation that's making it so hard for you to cope, and how you think you would handle a similar situation in the future?

What makes this current situation so difficult is that everything hit me at once—losing the promised job happened right as my student loans were coming due and my lease was ending, leaving me with absolutely no safety net. In the future, once I have a stable job and a solid plan, I won't have this extreme baseline of insecurity, so a setback wouldn't feel like my entire life is collapsing.

Do you think your current emotional state is a direct result of the accumulation of stressors, such as the job loss, financial issues, and housing uncertainty, or do you feel that there's an underlying issue that's making you more vulnerable to these stressors?

I definitely feel it's a direct result of all these stressors hitting me at once, rather than any underlying issue. This reaction feels temporary and completely tied to everything being up in the air right now. Once I can secure a stable job or housing plan, I'm confident I will be able to recover and cope normally again.
